# Sweet Confections by Kelsey

> Licensed and insured home bakery in Pittsfield, Massachusetts (Berkshire County), run by baker Kelsey Hecht. Everything is baked from scratch — custom celebration cakes, wedding cakes, cupcakes, cookies, brownies, cinnamon buns, chocolate-dipped strawberries, brunch boxes, and scratch-made frozen custard. Pickup in Pittsfield, MA, with delivery across the Berkshires, Western Massachusetts, Eastern New York, Southern Vermont, and Northwest Connecticut (roughly a 1–2 hour radius). 5.0-star rated by customers on Google and Facebook.

Key facts:

- Business: Sweet Confections by Kelsey, a licensed & insured home bakery (fully custom, made-to-order — no storefront)
- Location: Pittsfield, MA 01201, in the Berkshires
- Service area: Berkshire County MA (Pittsfield, Lenox, Stockbridge, Lee, Great Barrington, Williamstown, North Adams and surrounding towns), Western MA (Northampton, Springfield), Eastern NY (Albany, Troy, Hudson), Southern VT (Bennington, Manchester), Northwest CT (Salisbury, Litchfield)
- Contact: sctreatsshop@gmail.com · (413) 358-8556 · https://sctreatsbakery.com
- Social: https://www.facebook.com/SweetConfectionsShop/ · https://www.instagram.com/sctreatsbakery/
- Ordering: request-based — customers submit an order request online and Kelsey confirms availability, final pricing, and pickup/delivery within 24 hours. Orders can be placed from anywhere (out-of-state gift orders for local recipients are common).
- Lead times: cookies, brownies, cupcakes, and most treats 24–48 hours; custom cakes about 1 week; wedding/event packages and cake bars 2–4 weeks
- Prices: custom celebration cakes from $70, themed character cakes from $75, wedding/event cakes from $120, smash cake + cupcake set from $55, cupcakes from $30/dozen, Build Your Own Brunch Box from $28, frozen custard $14/pint, Build-Your-Own Cake Bar event packages $150–$250, wedding cake bar packages $1,100–$1,950
- Frozen custard: scratch-made, $14 per pint, rotating flavors — Holy Crumbs (homemade vanilla custard with homemade chocolate chip cookie pieces, brownie pieces, vanilla crumble, and cookie butter), Blueberry Cobbler, Peach Cobbler, Apple Cobbler, Peanut Butter & Banana, Milk Chocolate — with new flavors announced on Facebook
- 14 scratch-made cake flavors and 14 frostings; gluten-free cake flavors available on request
- A dessert food truck is in the works, targeting a 2026 launch

## Guides

- [Baking Notes & Ordering Guides](https://sctreatsbakery.com/blog.html): index of ordering guides
- [How Much Does a Wedding Cake Cost in the Berkshires?](https://sctreatsbakery.com/blog-wedding-cake-cost.html): what drives wedding cake pricing (servings, design complexity, flavors, delivery distance), real starting prices, cake bar package pricing, 50% deposit terms, and ways to reduce cost
- [How Far in Advance Should You Order a Custom Cake?](https://sctreatsbakery.com/blog-how-far-in-advance.html): lead times by product (24–48 hours for treats, ~1 week for custom cakes, 2–4 weeks for weddings/events), rush order guidance, and what details to include when ordering
- [Wedding Cake Delivery to Berkshires Venues](https://sctreatsbakery.com/blog-berkshires-wedding-venues.html): delivering wedding cakes to venues in Lenox (Tanglewood, The Mount, Wheatleigh, Blantyre, Miraval Berkshires), Stockbridge (Red Lion Inn), Lee (Devonfield Inn), and Great Barrington (Thornewood Inn), plus venue logistics and what to confirm
- [Cake Delivery in Lenox, Richmond, and the Towns Around Pittsfield](https://sctreatsbakery.com/blog-cake-delivery-towns.html): delivery coverage town by town across Berkshire County and into Western MA, Eastern NY, Southern VT, and Northwest CT; pickup vs. delivery; short-notice guidance
- [How to Send a Cake to Someone in the Berkshires](https://sctreatsbakery.com/blog-send-cake-gift.html): ordering a surprise cake or treat box from out of state — steps, gift messages, keeping the surprise, timing
- [How Much Cake Do I Need? A Serving Size Guide](https://sctreatsbakery.com/blog-cake-serving-sizes.html): servings by cake size (6" ~12, 8" 20 party/24 wedding, 10" 28/38, 12" 40/56), party vs wedding slice, tier combinations, factors that change the count
- [How to Store and Transport a Cake Without Ruining It](https://sctreatsbakery.com/blog-store-transport-cake.html): car transport, refrigerate or not, how early to pick up, leftovers and freezing
- [Gluten-Free Cakes: What to Know Before You Order](https://sctreatsbakery.com/blog-gluten-free-cakes.html): the 10 gluten-free cake flavors, additional charge, and honest cross-contact disclosure (shared kitchen, not celiac-safe)
- [The First Birthday Smash Cake: A Complete Guide](https://sctreatsbakery.com/blog-smash-cake-guide.html): size, timing around naps and meals, mild flavors, photo setup, the $55 smash cake + cupcake set
- [Baby Shower Dessert Ideas That Aren't Just Cake](https://sctreatsbakery.com/blog-baby-shower-desserts.html): dessert table combinations with prices, quantity rules of thumb, gender reveal logistics
- [Cupcakes or Cake? How to Decide for Your Party](https://sctreatsbakery.com/blog-cupcakes-vs-cake.html): serving logistics, cost comparison, when each wins, and the small-cake-plus-cupcakes hybrid
- [Ordering Holiday Desserts in the Berkshires: A Timeline](https://sctreatsbakery.com/blog-holiday-dessert-ordering.html): which weeks fill first for Thanksgiving and Christmas, what travels to a hosted dinner, seasonal flavors
- [Buttercream vs. Fondant: Which Should You Choose?](https://sctreatsbakery.com/blog-buttercream-vs-fondant.html): taste, sharp edges, heat tolerance, cost, and the hybrid approach
- [How to Choose Cake Flavors Everyone Will Actually Eat](https://sctreatsbakery.com/blog-choosing-cake-flavors.html): all 14 cake flavors, 14 frostings, 5 drizzles, pairings that work, using multiple flavors across tiers
- [What a Licensed Home Bakery Actually Means](https://sctreatsbakery.com/blog-licensed-home-bakery.html): what licensing and insurance cover, allergen limits of a shared kitchen, questions to ask any bakery
- [Frozen Custard vs. Ice Cream: What's the Difference?](https://sctreatsbakery.com/blog-frozen-custard-vs-ice-cream.html): frozen custard requires at least 1.4% egg yolk solids (both require 10% milkfat) and is churned with less air/overrun, making it denser and silkier; includes current custard flavors
